title: o says /o/
parentNote: Today is the third vowel, and vowels are the hinge every word turns on — with o added, hundreds of new words open up at once: not, hot, rock, chop, dog. The mistake is almost always the letter's name: children who have learnt that this letter is called "oh" will read "not" as "note" and "hop" as "hope". Names are for later; today it only ever says /o/, the sound at the start of otter, with the mouth open and round like a little cave. The other thing to listen for is o and a getting swapped, so "hot" comes out "hat" — say the pair back to back a few times and let them watch your jaw drop on the o.

activities.mouthCue: Open your mouth round and wide and let your jaw drop. Your tongue stays right down at the bottom.
activities.prompt: A brand new vowel. Its name is oh, but the sound it makes is o.
Two vowels, both with the mouth open. One is round, one is wide and flat. Find the round one.
All three vowels you know. Listen for the one with the jaw right down.
Three sounds, and the new one is in the middle. Keep it short — not note.
Only the first sound has changed. Keep the middle exactly the same.
The new vowel with an old team at the end. Still three sounds.
A team at the front and the new vowel behind it.
This is the big one today. Same start, same ending — the middle is the whole word.
Round mouth or smiling mouth? Listen to the middle.
Two vowels that look nothing alike but sit in the same spot. Which one is this?

activities.text: The cat sat on the hot rock.
Pam got a mop and did the job.
Did the chick hop in the pot?

activities.title: The dog on the log
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Tom did chop at the big log.
Tom can not chop with the dog on it!
The dog got off and Tom did chop the log.
